scenarios.name: Bull – AI Burn-In Standard + SiC Recovery
scenarios.notes: Wafer-level burn-in becomes standard for AI accelerator reliability screening (lead hyperscaler ramps, second AI supplier converts); SiC recovers on 200mm transition and 800V datacenter power; HBM/memory WLBI lands. Revenue ~$500M by FY2031.

scenarios.name: Base – Guide Met, Then Deceleration
scenarios.notes: FY2027 guide ($130-150M) met on $100M effective backlog; AI burn-in niche grows but stays concentrated in 1-2 hyperscale customers; SiC slow recovery through the 2027-28 overcapacity correction; growth decelerates to mid-teens after FY2027.

scenarios.name: Bear – Backlog Evaporates / Burn-In Intensity Falls
scenarios.notes: Cancellable backlog slips (10-K warns POs are cancellable with limited penalties); lead AI customer insources or qualifies a competitor; device yield improvements cut burn-in intensity; SiC glut persists past 2028. Re-rating to cyclical multiple.

evidence_for: Backlog $80.6M at FYE2026 vs $15.2M prior year (5.3x), effective backlog $100.6M incl. post-quarter bookings [10-K FY2026; Q4 release 2026-07-14].
FY2027 guidance $130-150M revenue (~2.6-3x) with 18-22% non-GAAP net margin [Q4 FY2026 release].
Customer diversification is real: top customer 67.3% (FY2024) to 26.3% (FY2026); three customers >10% [10-K FY2026 Item 1].
AI order momentum: $41M Sonoma (Apr 2026), $22M AI WLBI (Aug 2026), ~$6M follow-on for a second AI processor (Oct 2026); two silicon photonics customers ramping.
evidence_against: Valuation ~90x guided forward non-GAAP earnings and ~55x trailing sales at $80.10; +245% over 52 weeks; 16% short interest [stockanalysis.com 2026-10-12].
GAAP-loss-making in FY2025-FY2026 (diluted EPS -$0.13, -$0.23); gross margin fell 49.1% to 35.3% over two years [10-K FY2026].
Backlog is cancellable/reschedulable with limited penalties per 10-K risk factors; the FY2027 guide rests on it.
Cash position is dilution-funded: +$97.2M FY2026 financing from ATM sales; new S-3 shelf filed Aug 2026 (terms unverified).
Structural category risk: customer yield improvements or sampling (vs 100% burn-in) reduce demand [10-K Item 1A].
SiC overcapacity expected to persist until 2027-2028 (Yole via PCIM 2026-07-29).
open_questions: Does Q1 FY2027 (prints 2026-11-02) show revenue run-rate consistent with the $130-150M guide?
Identity and ownership of the lead hyperscale AI customer relationships; durability past the second processor generation.
Aug 2026 S-3 shelf size/terms and dilution intent.
Named wafer-level burn-in competitors and whether the 'only vendor offering both' claim holds.
Deceased officer identity and key-person exposure (Sep 2026 proxy).

predictions.notes: First checkpoint against the FY2027 guide; $130M low end implies ~$32.5M quarterly average with ramp, so Q1 below $25M would signal slippage.

predictions.claim: FY2027 revenue (year ending 2027-06-25) lands >= $130M, the guidance low end
predictions.notes: Backed by $100.6M effective backlog; main risk is backlog cancellation/rescheduling disclosed in the 10-K.

predictions.claim: No single customer exceeds 30% of revenue in the FY2027 10-K
predictions.notes: Top customer was 26.3% in FY2026 with three customers >10%; AI ramp could re-concentrate revenue into the lead hyperscale account.

predictions.claim: The benchmarked 'major supplier of AI accelerators, CPUs, and network processors' places a production (pilot or volume) order by mid-2027
predictions.notes: Benchmark 'exceeded expectations' per Q4 FY2026 release; conversion would de-risk single-thread AI exposure.

decision_journal.situation: AEHR at $80.10 (~$2.61B cap) trades at ~90x guided FY2027 non-GAAP EPS (~$0.85 midpoint) after +245% in 52 weeks. Scenario-weighted 5-year expected CAGR is ~-0.5% from this entry; the market has pre-paid the bull case. Business momentum (backlog 5.3x, AI order cadence, diversification 67%->26% top customer) is genuinely strong.
alternatives_rejected: Initiate a starter position at $80 (rejected: negative scenario-weighted expected return at this entry; Kelly sizing is zero).
Wait for a post-earnings dip mechanically (rejected: no dip may come if Q1 confirms; the entry rule is price-based, not event-timing-based).
Drop coverage as too expensive (rejected: story quality and engine value of a tracked belief state justify watchlist tracking with dated predictions).
